_comment: npm dependency policy fixture — DISALLOWED LICENSE (issue #1349). This file documents what check-licenses.js outputs when a package uses a license not in allowed-licenses.json. It is NOT a real package.json entry — it is a human-readable test fixture used by dep-policy.yml to verify that CI correctly identifies the dependency, version, source, and violation.

simulatedPackage.name: evil-gpl-package
simulatedPackage.description: Hypothetical package whose GPL-3.0 license is not on the approved list.

expectedOutput:
[license-check] FAIL — 1 license violation(s):
  evil-gpl-package@2.0.0  license=GPL-3.0-only  source=https://registry.npmjs.org/evil-gpl-package  violation=disallowed-license
mitigation: To add an approved exception, add an entry to celo-contracts/allowed-licenses.json under 'allowedExceptions' with 'name', 'version', 'license', 'reason', 'reviewedDate', 'expires', and 'issue' fields, then open a PR for review. See docs/dependency-policy.md.
